newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro sees $2 bln 1997 consolidated sales.
newsitem.headline: Vitro sees $2 bln 1997 consolidated sales.

text.p: Mexican glass firm Vitro SA sees 1997 consolidated sales of about $2 billion, the company's finance director said Friday.

"Anchor Glass represents about a third of the sales of Vitro," Vitro's corporate finance director Hugo Jaime Garcia said, speaking after the company's announcement that it will sell its subsidiary Anchor Glass Corp.
"We are talking about a company one-third smaller, so our sales could be around $2 billion."

Vitro said earlier Friday it had reached a non-binding agreement with Ball-Foster Container Co to sell Anchor for an estimated $365 million. In addition, Ball-Foster would assume Anchor's main liabilities, analysts said.
Anchor filed for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code and will thus be able to continue operating while the deal is being finalized, analysts said.
Garcia spoke at a news conference, where Vitro officials also said Vitro's total debt of about $2.3 billion would fall to about $1.7 billion without Anchor.
